text:
maria: Heads up — customer on Dedicated reported CI started failing right after our tagged release v1.2.0. Their GitLab CI shows a 401 when `go` tries to fetch github.com/redwood/llm@v1.2.0 from their private GOPROXY. Repro steps they gave:

1) checkout app repo
2) CI runs `GO111MODULE=on` with GOPRIVATE=github.com/redwood/* and GOPROXY=https://goproxy.internal
3) go build -> error:
`go: github.com/redwood/llm@v1.2.0: reading github.com/redwood/llm/go.mod at revision v1.2.0: 401 Unauthorized`

I asked them to paste the go.mod that triggered the tag; they attached this snippet from the tagged commit:

```
module github.com/redwood/llm

require (
    github.com/some/dep v0.3.0
)

replace github.com/redwood/llm => ../llm
```

sam: Ugh. Can you confirm the tag actually points at a commit with that replace present? 401 suggests the private proxy failed auth while trying to fetch the VCS/zip — could be proxy hitting the git host and being rejected. :thinking:

maria: Yes, tag v1.2.0 references the commit that still had the local replace. The customer says before the tag everything was fine, CI failed only after they pulled in v1.2.0. If we published a tag pointing to a tree with a filesystem replace, some proxies/clients behave oddly instead of returning 404.

ben: That would explain it. If the module path in the tag points to an on-disk replace, `go` may attempt VCS lookups that the proxy then forwards to the git host with the CI's token and the host responds 401. The root cause is the release including a replace directive that references a relative filesystem path.

sam: Short-term workaround: ask customer to set `GOPROXY=direct` or `GOPROXY=https://proxy.golang.org,direct` for the CI run to bypass the private proxy, then `go get github.com/redwood/llm@v1.2.1` once we cut a fixed release. Also they can pin to an earlier working tag.

maria: They tried `GOPROXY=direct` and the build passed. They've asked if we can unpublish v1.2.0 — we can't unpublish, but we can push v1.2.1 and recommend they pin or update CI. I've shared the tag->commit diff with them.

deploy-bot: release-bot created PR #987 to cut v1.2.1 removing the local replace in go.mod.

ben: I'll land the patch. After release let's add a CI lint that fails any tagged commit that contains `replace .*=> \.{2}/` in go.mod (grep or go list) to prevent local filesystem replaces from being included in releases.

sam: :thumbsup: Also add a post-release note in the changelog explaining the fix and the recommended temporary CI workaround for customers that hit the proxy 401.

maria: Thanks — forwarding this to the customer now.
